prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1239; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer's narrative: On the afternoon of the reported incident, I responded to a rear-end collision on a commercial stretch of road in Katy, Texas. Driver 1 was stopped in traffic when the vehicle behind struck the rear bumper of Driver 1's car. Driver 2 was the operator of the striking vehicle and stated that traffic ahead had stopped suddenly. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and said the impact pushed the head forward and back, which is consistent with the injuries described. A Passenger was seated in the front right position of Driver 1's vehicle and was present at the scene, and both the Passenger and Driver 1 confirmed this to me. I reviewed the scene photographs, which show the rear damage on Driver 1's vehicle lining up with the impact from Driver 2's front end. No earlier damage to either vehicle was known to the parties. No independent witnesses came forward. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved. Both drivers were cooperative, and no citations were issued at the scene pending further review.
